newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea threatens again to "punish" south.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea threatens again to "punish" south.

text.p: North Korea vowed again on Saturday to punish Seoul for the deaths of its soldiers who landed by submarine in South Korea last month.

Pyongyang also accused Seoul of conspiring to ignite war on the tense Korean peninsula and demanded it cancel plans for annual joint military exercices with the United States, scheduled for later this month.

In a communique carried by the official Korea Central News Agency (KCNA), North Korea blamed the southern government of Kim Young-sam for worsening tensions on the peninsula over the submarine incident.

Twenty-two of the 26 North Korean soldiers who came ashore from the submarine last month have been killed by South Korean troops or found dead, while one has been captured alive and a hunt is on for the remaining three.
"We will certainly punish the Kim Young-sam group, the very one who fabricated the incident, and make them pay for the blood," the KCNA report said.

Pyongyang, which says the submarine drifted into South Korean waters after developing engine trouble on a training mission, demands Seoul return the bodies along with survivors and the vessel while threatening "merciless retaliation" for the deaths.
"The longer the Kim Young-sam group delay the return of our submarine, survivors and the corpses, the more strained the situation on the Korean peninsula will be," KCNA said.
Seoul says the submarine was dropping off armed commandos in a prelude to wider military action.

On Saturday, South Korea's 299-seat National Assembly, in which Kim's ruling party has a slim majority, adopted a resolution denouncing the incursion, asking the government to strengthen national security and demanding Pyongyang apologise.
"We urge the North Korean regime to immediately revoke its threat to retaliate," the assembly said in the resolution.
Tensions on the peninsula, where a fragile ceasefire has kept the peace since the end of the 1950-53 Korean War, have escalated in recent weeks.
The crisis flared again this week after the murder of three villagers in the east coast Mount Odae area.
Seoul suspects the remaining North Korean infiltrators killed the trio and has ordered thousands of soldiers to the area to hunt down the fugitives.
In a separate KCNA dispatch, Pyongyang said plans for annual U.S.-South Korean joint military exercises, codenamed Foal Eagle '96, were an "unbearable challenge and provocation" against the north.
"The Kim Young-sam bellicose group's war frenzy has reached a very extreme stage. They intend to ignite a war against the north in conspiracy with outside forces," it said.
"They must immediately cancel the plan of Foal Eagle and all other provocative military exercises against the north."

The carrier USS Independence and the majority of South Korean and U.S. troops stationed in South Korea plan to participate in Foal Eagle, which involves the firing of blank ammunition and night combat exercises.
The drills are to run from October 28 to November 20.
The United States stations 37,000 servicemen in South Korea to support the 655,000-strong South Korean military.
